findings.summary: The owner-override arm window used Date.now() (wall clock) rather than a monotonic clock, so a system clock adjustment between arming and a repeat (sleep/resume, an NTP correction) could stretch or shrink the 20s confirmation window.
findings.disposition: fixed before commit -- switched to performance.now(); ART-20260906-051/052 re-versioned to ART-20260906-053/054 (v2) to bring it into scope

findings.summary: pendingAssign holds one arm at a time, so cycling through several unavailable owners in quick succession can leave up to four stale 20-second toasts visible while only the most recent combination is actually armed.
findings.disposition: accepted, not fixed -- repeating an older visible toast's combination safely re-arms rather than silently confirming, so this is a readability nuance, not a correctness defect; recorded in ART-20260906-053's scope_out
